websocket_next_flow.conclusion: Yes. A WebSocket upgrade (GET + Connection: upgrade + Upgrade: websocket) whose raw path matches an app.ws route is sent by Dispatcher.handle to handleLegacy, which runs the legacy MiddlewarePipeline: global middleware plus every prefix middleware registered through app.use(String prefix, mw), in registration order, and then a terminal that only records `reached`; after pipeline.run returns with the response still NEW, the upgrade runs. Middleware never interleaves with the ws route, so a proxy mounted with app.use("/api/orders", proxy) always runs before app.ws("/api/orders/live") regardless of registration order, and calling next.run() reaches the terminal and the upgrade; answering instead hides the ws route. Caveats: (1) only app.use(String, Middleware) registrations join the legacy pipeline; app.use(Object path, mw) (Express path patterns) and child Routers do not, so such middleware never sees WS upgrades; (2) addCommonPrefix silently skips prefixes that are not representable in the strict WS decoded profile; (3) on this path DefaultRequest is built with commonHttp=false, so req.baseUrl() is "" and req.path() is the decoded full path (irrelevant if the proxy calls next() before using them); (4) a WS upgrade with no matching app.ws route goes through the common HTTP path (HttpExecution), where next() continues to later layers and ends in FinalHandler (404).

risks.description: Name/visibility collision: DefaultRequest already has package-private `InputStream bodyStream()`; adding public Request.bodyStream() fails to compile until the internal method (and its callers JsonBodyReader:41, DefaultRequest:286/295) is renamed.

Adapter body streams throw unchecked HttpException(413/408/400) from read() on TinyHttpd (transport limits, timeouts, truncation), so reads of bodyStream are not IOException-only as A-1 assumes; the proxy's body-copy loop must also catch RuntimeException and close the backend. On servlet, any read IOException aborts the whole exchange, so a client-side read failure cannot produce a 4xx there.
relay via startBody would still emit Content-Length for 204 and would apply defaultCache in begin(); both need explicit handling (prepare() drops Content-Length for 204/304, startBody does not).
Public API surface tests assert exact method sets for Request, Response and RestApp and the configurable-method list; every new method must be added there test-first or the build breaks.

Moving BodyTooLargeException breaks internal imports (LimitedInputStream, FormBodyReader, MultipartParser, two tests) and introduces a same-simple-name class to TinyHttpd's com.snoworca.tinyhttpd.http.BodyTooLargeException used in the adapter; also changes StandardErrors.statusOf so DefaultRequest.logFailure stops logging it as a 500.

rawBodyLimit plumbing: Dispatcher has a 6-deep telescoping constructor chain used by ~15 test call sites and DefaultRequest has 5 public constructors; adding a parameter ripples widely. A package setter (like Dispatcher.proxyTrust / DefaultRequest.proxyTrust) set at freeze avoids that.

res.onAbort: client-disconnect notification reaches DefaultResponse.abort only through HttpExecution (common HTTP path) and adapters that override HttpExchange.onAbort; the in-memory test adapter and custom adapters do not notify, and the legacy (WS) dispatch path never registers. Firing listeners from DefaultResponse.abort (no-op once COMPLETED) gives the requested once-only, not-on-success semantics.

WebSocket pass-through depends on registration via app.use(String, mw): app.use(Object path, mw) does not join the legacy pipeline, and unrepresentable prefixes are skipped silently, so a proxy mounted that way never sees upgrades (harmless) but tests for AC-B12 must use the String overload.
